newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end stronger with U.S. on CPI data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end stronger with U.S. on CPI data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger in active trade on Tuesday, firming with U.S. Treasuries after a consumer price report showed U.S. inflation pressures remained subdued, analysts said.

"It was the very positive response to the U.S. CPI release that had the major hand in propelling the Canadian market to the gains we've seen today," said Arve Bendiksrud, a fixed-income analyst with TD Securities Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$1.00 to C$108.00 to yield 7.308 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond rose 31/32 to yield 7.09 percent.
The spread between the two bonds widened to 22 basis points, unchanged from the close on Monday.

Canadian bonds strengthened after the U.S. March consumer price index allayed market fears of an acceleration in price growth. The move sparked a rally in U.S. debt markets and was seen easing the pressure on Federal Reserve policymakers to raise interest rates there.

Speculation that the Federal Reserve would be less willing to raise rates also boosted the Canadian dollar, which further supported bonds. But the dollar gave up most of those gains by the end of the session.

In new issue news, the Canadian government today announced the launch of its Euro Medium-Term Note program, which is designed to diversify the source of funding for Canada's foreign exchange reserves.

The amount of money to be borrowed under the program was not disclosed. A Finance Department official told Reuters the department did not yet have a specific target for how much it would like to borrow under the program, but that it was not foreseen to be more than US$3 billion.
In other prices, the Canadian 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.68 to C$101.48 to yield 6.786 percent.
The U.S. bond rose 24/32 to yield 6.87 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to eight basis points from 10 basis points on Monday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.19 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.29 percent.

The Bank of Canada conducted one round of special purchase and resale agreements in the money market at 3.25 percent late in the session. The central bank intervened to add liquidity to the market after the call loan or overnight lending rate was bid at 3.25 percent, the top of the Bank of Canada's target range for the rate.
